newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-HAGEMEYER NET SURGES, SEES SALES JUMP.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-HAGEMEYER NET SURGES, SEES SALES JUMP.

text.p: Dutch trading group Hagemeyer NV said on Wednesday its 1996 turnover and profits rose sharply, boosted by the consolidation of former rival Borsumij Wehry which it bought in 1995.
Net profit surged 47.5 percent to 285.2 million guilders in 1996, with turnover up by 43.6 percent to 8.22 billion guilders.
The group, in which Hong Kong's First Pacific Co has a controlling stake, said it expected profits and earnings per share to show a further increase in 1997.
Hagemeyer will pay a dividend of 2.28 guilders per share for last year and plans a two-for-one share split.
In Amsterdam, Hagemeyer stock closed 2.60 guilders higher at 165.50 apiece.
The group said that organic growth of 4.6 percent fell short of expectations last year, but it did complete a number of smaller acquisitions.
Hagemeyer chairman Andrew Land told a news conference that the group's earlier fears on a downturn in consumer electronics had been confirmed.
"Turnover from consumer electronics will probably be less than six percent of total 1997 turnover, compared to 31 percent in 1993."
But he was more upbeat on future turnover growth, saying he expected an increase in turnover to 11-12 billion guilders within the next few years.
"We're aiming for an increase of 12-15 percent annually, partly through acquisitions," Land said, adding that half the growth would be organic and the remainder through takeovers.
Hagemeyer generates about 60 percent of its turnover in Europe, 20 percent in the Americas and 20 percent in Asia.
Land said that within five years, half the group's sales should come from Europe, with the other 50 percent more or less evenly divided between the Americas and Asia.
He said the group would continue to seek acquisitions in Asia and the United States, but did not elaborate.
Land also said Hagemeyer was planning an Asian bourse listing for its Hagemeyer Cosa Liebermann (HCL) unit, but said the group would continue to hold a majority stake in HCL.
The group's consumer and professional products group achieved a significant increase in turnover last year, helped by the consolidation of 70 percent-owned retailer Ceteco and other ventures.
Electrical distribution maintained its upward trend of recent years.
"In general, operational results met our standards," Hagemeyer said, adding that both gross margins and cost levels were higher than in 1995.
Associates' income surged to 45 million guilders from 12.6 million in 1995, reflecting acquisitions and higher contributions from investments.
